candidate_relations.reason: Basal ganglia disease localizes the T1-hyperintense striatum but omits nonketotic hyperglycemic hemichorea.
Hyperglycemia-induced choreoathetosis is an accepted alias of nonketotic hyperglycemia hemichorea in untreated diabetes with striatal T1 hyperintensity.
Dyskinesia is a compatible movement-disorder parent but lacks the nonketotic hyperglycemic hemichorea specification.
Diabetic hemichorea is the same diagnostic object as nonketotic hyperglycemia hemichorea with unilateral chorea and striatal T1 hyperintensity.
Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation is a different chronic basal-ganglia disease, not acute diabetic hemichorea.
Diabetic striatal disease denotes the same striatopathy that produces nonketotic hyperglycemia hemichorea.
Diabetic complications is a compatible parent category missing the specific nonketotic hyperglycemic hemichorea syndrome.
Hyperglycemic hemichorea is a wording variant of nonketotic hyperglycemia hemichorea in this diabetic striatal T1-hyperintensity presentation.
Movement disorder is a broad compatible parent without the hyperglycemic hemichorea etiology and laterality.
Hemichorea describes the phenomenology but omits the nonketotic hyperglycemic cause required by the reference.
Huntington disease is a different hereditary chorea and does not produce this acute diabetic striatal T1 hyperintensity.

case_quality_flags: Ketones are not reported; glucose is only modestly elevated though T1 striatal hyperintensity and hemichorea are classic
